messages:
maya: Hey — seeing a short but sharp bump in 5xx for /v1/generate over the last 15m, mostly 502/504 timeouts. Where's the best place to pull route-level metrics, logs and traces to triage? I opened a quick graph but couldn't split by route. Anyone?

raj: Start with the API Error Breakdown grafana (has route var): https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/err/api-error-breakdown?var-route=/v1/generate — and the per-route latency heatmap: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/lat/route-heatmap?var-route=/v1/generate. Those cover rates + percentiles.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: gateway/502-rate-spike for /v1/generate at 1799002470. Incident template: https://confluence.redwood/ops/incidents/502-spike-template 

emily: For logs use Kibana with this quick query (last 30m):
`service:gateway AND http.path:"/v1/generate" AND status:[500 TO 599]`
Quick discover link (paste into browser): https://kibana.internal.redwood/app/discover#/?_a=(query:(query_string:(query:'service:gateway%20AND%20http.path:"/v1/generate"%20AND%20status:[500%20TO%20599]')))

chris: For traces check Honeycomb/Jaeger: dataset = redwood-traces, query: `trace.http.path = "/v1/generate" AND http.status_code >= 500` — that should give spans where upstream timed out. Also run this Prometheus query to see error rate broken down by code: 
```
sum by (code) (rate(redwood_http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",job="gateway"}[5m]))
```

maya: thanks — curious about alert noise. current policy fires when >0.5% 5xx for 5m and it's been noisy around deploy windows. Any recommended thresholds?

raj: We typically use two layers: fast noisy detection for oncall (e.g. >1% 5xx for 3m) and a sustained alert for business impact (e.g. >0.5% for 15m). Also add a CI/deploy suppression label or a short maintenance window during rollout. See playbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/alerts/5xx-tuning 

emily: If it's timeouts specifically, check envoy timeout metrics: `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_timeouts{cluster=~"gateway.*"}` and backend logs for \"context deadline exceeded\". Also check upstream host distribution in logs — if traffic shifted to a misbehaving host you'll see skewed 5xx counts.

chris: Another quick triage: pull a few sample trace IDs from the Kibana logs (search for "trace_id") then load them in Honeycomb to inspect downstream spans. Example curl to fetch traces (replace $HONEY_KEY):
```
curl -s -H \"X-API-Key: $HONEY_KEY\" \"https://api.honeycomb.io/1/traces?query=trace.http.path%3D%22%2Fv1%2Fgenerate%22%20AND%20http.status_code%3E%3D500&limit=50\"
```

maya: I'll pull logs + 3 trace ids and post back here. Can someone add the grafana panel snapshot to the incident doc and pin the Kibana query? :wave:

raj: on it — adding the panel snapshot and linking the kibana query to the incident doc now. :thumbsup: 

emily: If you want a quick mitigation while triaging, consider temporarily bumping the gateway upstream timeout to avoid cascading 504s, or enable the canary fallback to the smaller model variant for a subset of traffic. Both are short-term risk mitigations.

chris: Also add a note to check dedicated GPU queue lengths and pod CPU steal/oom events — overload there can manifest as gateway 502/504s. Happy to help look at traces once you post ids.

maya: Great — filing results in the incident doc in ~15m. Thanks team!
